newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on technical slide, Egypt.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on technical slide, Egypt.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on signs the market was technically overbought and some traders cited disappointment in the amount of wheat sold to Egypt by the U.S.

Egypt over the weekend bought at least 200,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat. Some traders called the amount disappointing, after talk circulated late last week that Egypt might buy as much as 500,000 to one million tonnes.
However, other traders said Egypt may buy more U.S. wheat this week.
Also there were expectations Pakistan this week will buy U.S. wheat, the traders said.
Traders also said showers in portions of Australia's wheat growing region may have weighed on the wheat market.

Technical indicators showed the wheat market was becoming overbought for the near term and due for at least a temporary correction. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the September contract rose to 73 percent Friday and closed at 70 percent Monday. An RSI of 70 or more is considered an overbought signal.
CBOT soft red winter wheat closed unchanged to 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down one at $3.57-1/2.
USDA Monday said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended July 24 totalled 18.795 million bushels. That figure was below the 22.436 million inspected the previous week.

Cargill Inc sold two million bushels of September, bought two million December and sold 1.5 million December, traders said. Continental Grain bought one half million December and sold 1.5 million December and Merrill Lynch Futures bought two million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 15,000 contracts, below the 20,654 traded Friday.

In wheat options, SAK Futures sold 100 September $3.40 calls at 24-3/4 to 25 cents, LFG Futures bought 250 December $4.00 calls at 13 cents and E.D. and F. Man International bought 100 March $4.00 calls at 23-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, above the 6,292 traded Friday.
